title_tag: ServiceTitan Review (2026): Honest Cost & Who It's For
title: ServiceTitan: Powerful — and Not Built for You
meta: Honest ServiceTitan review for 2026: what it really costs (per-tech pricing, five-figure implementation, annual contracts), why it's built for large/franchise operations, and what small shops should run instead.
dek: ServiceTitan is the Ferrari of field-service software. It's genuinely powerful. It's also priced, contracted, and onboarded for franchise-scale operations — which means for a one-to-ten-truck shop it's usually the wrong, wildly expensive answer. Here's the honest math before a salesperson gets you on a 12-month contract.
verdict_text: Only if you're big. ServiceTitan is a serious platform for large, multi-crew, dispatch-heavy operations — and it bills like it: reportedly $245–$400+ per technician per month, a five-figure implementation fee, and a 12-month contract. For most small shops that's tens of thousands a year to use a fraction of it. Run Jobber or Housecall Pro instead and revisit ServiceTitan when you're genuinely scaling.

blocks.h: It's good. That's not the question.
blocks.html: Let's be fair: ServiceTitan is a deep, capable platform — dispatch, call booking, marketing attribution, payroll, reporting, the works. Big HVAC, plumbing, and electrical operations run their whole business on it for a reason. The question was never “is it good software.” It's “is it the right software for your shop” — and for most of the people reading this, the price and the contract answer that for you.

blocks.label: Slow down
blocks.claim: “The all-in-one platform to grow your business.”
blocks.small: It can grow a large business. But the per-tech pricing, the five-figure implementation, and the annual contract are built for franchise-scale operations. Below that scale, the setup fee alone is hard to earn back. Don't let a demo talk a two-truck shop onto a 12-month commitment it doesn't need.

notes.text: The per-tech cost, implementation fees, and long onboarding are designed for franchise and large multi-crew operations — not small shops.

blocks.src_note: ServiceTitan doesn't publish prices; figures are contractor-reported third-party estimates and vary by source. Get a written quote before signing anything.

workorder.h: We'll right-size your software — and your spend
workorder.p: Tell us your crew size and goals; we'll pick the platform that fits (usually not the five-figure one), set it up, and wire it to a site that sends you work — so you're not paying enterprise prices for a small-shop job.

ledger_note: The small-shop links are affiliate links — we may earn a commission at no cost to you. It never changes the verdict; we just told a small shop to skip the five-figure contract.

faq.q: How much does ServiceTitan cost in 2026?
faq.a: ServiceTitan doesn't publish prices, but contractors report roughly $245–$400+ per technician per month, a one-time implementation fee of about $5,000–$50,000, and a 12-month contract. For a 10-tech shop that's roughly $29,000–$48,000+ in year one for the subscription alone.

faq.q: Is ServiceTitan worth it for a small contractor?
faq.a: Usually not. It's built for large, multi-crew, franchise-scale operations, and the per-tech pricing plus five-figure setup is hard to earn back below that scale. Most small shops get the same core jobs done on Jobber or Housecall Pro for a fraction of the cost.

faq.q: What should a small shop use instead of ServiceTitan?
faq.a: Jobber for the cleanest, cheapest all-in-one, or Housecall Pro if you need built-in financing and multi-tech dispatch. Revisit ServiceTitan only when you're genuinely scaling into a large operation.
